The paper presents a deep-learning-enabled self-adaptive microwave cloak.
The cloak uses a metasurface with tunable unit cells.
The pretrained ANN is used to adjust the reflection spectrum of the metasurface cloak.
The metasurface cloak exhibits a millisecond response time.
The cloak can render objects invisible without human intervention.
The pretrained ANN was trained using ~10,000 measured samples.
The final MSE of the validation set is 3.22 × 10^−3.
The MREs of the three sets are all less than 2.1%.
The frequency of the incident wave is 8.4 GHz.
The polarization of the incident wave is transverse-magnetic (TM, or p-polarized).
The size of the metasurface inclusion is 180 × 210 × 2 mm^3 (24 × 28 unit cells).
The metasurface cloak uses a varactor diode to adjust its reflection spectrum.
The pretrained ANN is used to interpret the intricate and non-intuitive relationships among the cloaking structure, incoming light, and surrounding environment.
The metasurface cloak can be used for real-time applications involving moving objects and in situ environments.
The cloak can be used for a wide range of applications, including stealth vehicles and moving objects.
